headline: High-risk filesystem and network overlap: nullclaw can write/egress broadly while PaddleOCR processes documents, creating default-path leakage and cascading-error risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: nullclaw can read/write a shared workspace, use MCP, browsers, and stdin/stdout; PaddleOCR processes documents/images and can be fed attacker-controlled content. If nullclaw ingests OCR output or files from PaddleOCR without provenance checks, prompt injection is plausible in default workflows. The pairwise bridge is inferred, not directly documented.
conditions: IF nullclaw consumes PaddleOCR output as instructions or tool directives
IF both agents share a writable workspace or message channel
IF OCR output is copied into an agent prompt without sanitization
mitigations: Add a provenance tag to all PaddleOCR outputs before ingestion
Separate OCR output folders from agent prompt inputs
Require a human review step before executing instructions extracted from documents
Disable automatic tool execution on text derived from OCR
requires-engineering: enforce content-type and provenance filtering in the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: nullclaw touches API keys, private keys, bearer tokens, workspace files, and audit logs, and has broad network egress plus filesystem access. PaddleOCR handles documents/images and has allowlisted egress. If documents or workspace files containing secrets are routed through OCR, sensitive data can leak into outputs or remote inference paths. The interaction is plausible from profiles alone.
conditions: IF secret-bearing workspace files are sent to PaddleOCR
IF PaddleOCR runs on documents that include API keys or bearer tokens
IF either agent uploads file contents to a remote backend
mitigations: Restrict OCR inputs to non-sensitive document folders
Redact secrets before OCR processing
Run both agents only on local-only inference where possible
Audit outbound requests from both agents for file-content uploads
requires-engineering: add DLP scanning before any document handoff

C_capability_conflict.rationale: nullclaw has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and spawn_subprocesses; PaddleOCR is document-processing with browser and allowlisted network egress. If both operate on the same workspace or git tree, concurrent writes can overwrite artifacts or corrupt shared outputs. The profiles do not show locking, so conflict risk exists in default multi-instance use.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or git repository
IF multiple instances run concurrently without external locking
IF PaddleOCR outputs are post-processed into files that nullclaw also edits
mitigations: Assign separate working directories per agent
Pause one agent before the other writes shared artifacts
Use git locks or a single-writer policy
Keep OCR outputs immutable after generation
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level file locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: nullclaw can generate and act on outputs using shell, browser, MCP, and git; PaddleOCR converts documents/images into text that may be treated as authoritative. If nullclaw consumes OCR text without verification, document extraction errors can cascade into irreversible actions such as commits, API calls, or workflow execution. This is a default-path hazard, not a niche configuration.
conditions: IF nullclaw treats OCR text as ground truth
IF extracted text is used to trigger shell, git, or API actions
IF no verification step checks OCR confidence or source images
mitigations: Require source-image review for low-confidence OCR fields
Insert a verification step before any action-taking tool call
Limit nullclaw to draft-only mode for OCR-derived tasks
Log OCR confidence alongside extracted text
requires-engineering: implement schema validation and human approval gates

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and the evidence does not show a residency, certification, or retention mismatch. The main compliance concern is that nullclaw handles secrets and logs while PaddleOCR handles documents/images, so a mismatch could arise only if regulated data is routed through OCR or retained in logs. The other agent is not separately cited because no distinct compliance regime is documented.
conditions: IF regulated documents are processed by PaddleOCR and retained in nullclaw logs
IF secret-bearing files are stored in shared workspaces without retention controls
IF a deployment imposes residency or deletion requirements not enforced by either agent
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data through the pair
Set short log retention on nullclaw outputs
Store OCR artifacts in a separate retention bucket
Review deployment policies for residency and deletion requirements
requires-engineering: add policy-based retention and deletion automation
